definitions: To increase one's commitment to a particular strategy or course of action, especially one that is proving risky or unsuccessful.
To reinforce an existing position or belief, often in the face of opposition or doubt.
examples: Despite the losses, the company decided to double down on its investment in the new technology.
She chose to double down on her argument, presenting more evidence to support it.
The politician doubled down on his controversial statements after public criticism.
pastTenses: doubled down on (past simple), doubled down on (present perfect)
